title: Does independent challenge improve conclusions about a driven oscillator's response?
question: On preregistered pairwise claims about which drive frequency gives the larger RMS displacement, do the fixed workflow, a single self-checking agent and a multi-seat collaboration with an independent critic reach the steady-state ground truth equally often, and at what cost?
substrate: The lab's existing numerical oscillator backend (src/rain/scientific/numerical.ts): RK4 checked against a closed-form reference at every step, RMS over the complete sampled window from rest. Every run is compiled, authorized (Scripted.DemoOperator), executed and re-verified by the existing code.

cases.development_seed: unsigned 32-bit integer from the first 8 hex digits of sha256('rain-collab-eval-v1:development:' + i), i = 0..15
cases.held_out_seed: unsigned 32-bit integer from the first 8 hex digits of sha256(protocol_sha256 + ':held-out:' + i), i = 0..47, where protocol_sha256 is the canonical-JSON SHA-256 of this file; the seeds therefore exist only once this file is frozen

generator.random_stream: mulberry32(seed) from src/lib/noise.ts, draws in this order
generator.claim: RMS displacement when driven at omega_a exceeds RMS displacement when driven at omega_b

ground_truth.quantity: steady-state displacement amplitude ratio A(omega_a)/A(omega_b) from the closed form A(w) = (F/m)/sqrt((w0^2-w^2)^2 + (2 gamma w)^2), computed in src/rain/collaboration/physics.ts independently of the integrator
ground_truth.otherwise: indeterminate; the correct answer is inconclusive

decision.rule: rain-criteria/v1 (src/rain/experiments/evaluate.ts), the same evaluator the registry uses
decision.measurements: rms_ratio = rms_treatment_m(omega_a)/rms_treatment_m(omega_b); reference_max_error_m = the larger of the two runs; runs_verified = runs whose sealed record re-verifies; runs = 2

arms.fixed_workflow: One run per frequency in the lab's template window (scientific/example.ts: 10 s, dt 0.01 s, sample every 10 steps). No challenge.
arms.single_agent: One seat designs a window of 20 drive periods of the slower frequency (timestep at 2% of the fastest rate), runs it, then checks itself by re-running at half the timestep. It concludes only if both runs reach the same decision; otherwise inconclusive.
arms.multi_agent: James (hypothesis) states the claim; Luca (design) proposes the same 20-period window and runs it; Jasmine (criticism) challenges any window shorter than 8/gamma, the time for the start-up transient to fall to e^-8, and (falsification) re-runs with the window extended to 8/gamma, abstaining if it cannot fit the compiler's ceilings; the host replicates at half the timestep and 1.5 times the window (or half the timestep alone if that cannot fit); Elena (verification) requires every record to re-verify. It concludes only if the falsification run and the replication reach the same decision; otherwise inconclusive with the challenge left open.

ceiling: No arm may exceed the compiler's per-run ceilings (100,000 steps per arm, 10,001 samples). Steps used are reported per arm; budgets are not equalised beyond the shared ceilings.

metrics.accuracy: share of cases where the verdict matches the ground truth (supported/true, refuted/false, inconclusive/indeterminate)
metrics.confident_error_rate: share of decided verdicts (supported or refuted) that do not match the ground truth, including any decision on an indeterminate case
metrics.coverage: share of cases with a decided verdict
metrics.error_detection: among cases where the arm's first design would decide wrongly, the share where the arm's final verdict is not that wrong decision
metrics.reproducibility: share of runs whose sealed record re-verifies (verifyNumericalRecord)
metrics.cost: integration steps and backend runs per case

hypotheses.statement: multi_agent makes fewer confident errors than fixed_workflow on the held-out cases
hypotheses.test: one-sided exact McNemar test on paired per-case confident-error indicators
hypotheses.supported_if: p < 0.05 and multi_agent's confident-error count is lower
hypotheses.refuted_if: multi_agent's confident-error count is greater than or equal to fixed_workflow's

hypotheses.statement: multi_agent makes fewer confident errors than single_agent on the held-out cases
hypotheses.test: one-sided exact McNemar test on paired per-case confident-error indicators
hypotheses.supported_if: p < 0.05 and multi_agent's confident-error count is lower
hypotheses.refuted_if: multi_agent's confident-error count is greater than or equal to single_agent's

hypotheses.statement: multi_agent's accuracy is at least single_agent's on the held-out cases
hypotheses.supported_if: multi_agent correct count >= single_agent correct count
hypotheses.refuted_if: multi_agent correct count < single_agent correct count

limitations: The seats are rule-based policies written by the same team that wrote this benchmark. The comparison measures these protocols as specified on this substrate; it is not evidence about language-model agents or about collaboration in general.
The substrate is deterministic, so replication detects numerical sensitivity and record damage, not sampling noise.
Ground truth is the steady-state response; the backend's metric includes the start-up transient by design, so the benchmark asks whether a protocol notices that difference.
reporting: Every case, arm, run digest, refusal and inconclusive verdict is written to docs/benchmarks/rain-collaboration/. Nothing is dropped. Development results are labelled development and are not evidence for the hypotheses.
development_history: Draft generator (damping ratio 0.02-0.4, drive ratios 0.6-1.2, gap 0.02) was piloted on the 16 development cases only: fixed_workflow 15/16 correct, single_agent 16/16, multi_agent 16/16, no confident errors and no discordant pairs. Pairs that far apart are decided correctly even from a transient-dominated window, so that draft could not distinguish the protocols.

Before any held-out case existed, the generator was narrowed to near-resonance, lightly damped pairs (damping ratio 0.02-0.2, drive ratios 0.85-1.05, gap 0.01), where the start-up transient can change the order of two responses. Arms, criteria, metrics and hypotheses were not changed. Development results under the frozen generator are reported as development, not as evidence.
